On taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence placed before this Tribunal and on hearing arguments, my answers to the above issues as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.3:
To prove his case, petitioner himself entered into witness box and got examined as P.W.1.
In chief examination he reiterated petition averments.

To prove the accidental injuries and negligence on the part of opponent vehicle, he produced documents of FIR, first information, seizure panchanama, spot panchanama, IMV report wound certificate, final report and discharge summary at Ex.P.
On perusal of these documents it can be seen that accident has occurred on 26.10.2019.
One Chandan.N has given first information to police on 27.10.2019 i.e, after 1 day of the accident.

He stated in the first information that, on 26.10.2019 when he was near his house, he was informed through phone that his brotherinlaw Manjuanth, petitioner herein has met with accident and he is shifted to Siddaganga hospital, Tumukur.
After receiving the news of accident, he ran to hospital and found that his brotherinlaw sustained injuries to body.
On enquiry his brotherinlaw he found that one lorry driver of vehicle no.KA01AF2470 came from high speed in opposite direction and hit the vehicle of the petitioner.

That petitioner sustained injury to his right hand,
shoulder and nasal bone.
On the basis of said information Nelamangala police have registered crime no.418/2019 against the driver of Container lorry.

In the spot panchanama it is mentioned that,
road is 30ft wide, highway tar road.
As per the IMV report there is no damage to the lorry, but to the Manjunath T.R vs Sbi Gen Ins Co Ltd on 27 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31850574/
3 two wheeler head light mask right side scratch.
As per the wound certificate issued by (SCCH12) 7 MVC.No.7965/2019 Siddaganga hospital, injury no.2 which is nasal bone fracture is grievous injury.
In the said wound certificate history of the injury is not mentioned.
Further in the final report driver of the lorry found to be negligent and charge sheet is filed against him.
It is also noted in the charge sheet that, the said driver had no driving licence to drive the vehicle at the time of accident.
10. In the cross examination of P.W.1 he deposed that, opponent lorry driver has not given any signal to take the turn and turned the vehicle suddenly by which accident took place.
There is suggestion that, he has seen the said lorry from 20 30meter away, P.W.1 stated that the said driver was in high speed.
He denied that he himself was riding the vehicle in high speed.
He also denied that there is negligence on his part.
By making aforesaid suggestion, the involvement of aforesaid lorry is admitted in the above case.
When according to respondent no.2, petitioner has seen the lorry from 2030 meters away, the lorry was present at the spot.
Then it is for the driver of the lorry to explain how the accident took place.
In the present case, he has not appeared before the court, nor he is summoned at the hands of R.W.2.
Further accused in the criminal case has to questioned the FIR nor the final report.
When accused himself has not challenged, insurance company is not competent to take defence that petitioner was negligent at the time of riding the vehicle.
Neither there is document to show that petitioner was negligent nor there is eye witness to support the said contention.
Merely on the basis of assumption, court cannot come to the conclusion that petitioner was negligent, (SCCH12) 8 MVC.No.7965/2019 though such contention is taken in the written statement.

Therefore, in the opinion of this court on the basis of oral and documentary evidence I am of the opinion that, petitioner has proved that driver of the lorry bearing reg. no.KA01AF 2470 was negligent in driving the lorry.
Accordingly, I answer this issue in the Affirmative.
11. ISSUE NO.2 :
In view of above reasons petitioner is entitled for the compensation in view of accidental injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.
The quantum of compensation has to be determined now.
Respondent no.1 disputed the age of the petitioner in the written statement.
To prove his age petitioner has produced his aadhaar card at Ex.P.8.
It shows that he was born on 02.12.1993.
Accident took place on 26.11.2019.
In the cross examination of P.W.1 his age is not disputed,
Therefore, age of the petitioner is considered as 25 years at the time of accident.
12. 1st respondent disputed the occupation of the petitioner.

In respect of occupation it is stated that, he is a Finance Officer at Capital Finance, Chikkaballapura and he was earning Rs.13,000/
per month.
But no documents are produced by the petitioner.
The occupation is disputed in the cross examination.
P.W.1 stated that he was removed from the job and he cannot do any work as earlier.

Having regard to the year in which the accident took place and the place of residence of the petitioner and the cost of living, it is proper to adopt notional income of Rs.13,000/ per month in the present case.

Accordingly, (SCCH12) 9 MVC.No.7965/2019 notional income of Rs.13,000/
per month is considered as income of the petitioner.

13. In respect of permanent disability P.W.1 doctor stated that petitioner has sustained nasal bone fracture and right clavicle lateral 3rd fracture and according to the doctor he has right arm disability of 33% and whole body disability of
In the cross examination such assessment made by the doctor is disputed by the 1st respondent.

He relied upon the judgment in Jayaanth Kumar.B V/s Manjunath T.R vs Sbi Gen Ins Co Ltd on 27 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31850574/
4 M.J.Mahesh, MFA 1602/2016 Dt.29.06.2016 passed by the Hon'ble High Court of Ka
In the present case P.W.2 doctor.
In the present case, not only clavicle bone but also nasal bone got fractured, that requires consideration.

Another doctor by name Dr.Chaitanya Babu, who is dental surgeon has also filed affidavit and stated that petitioner has sustained nasal bone fracture and 4 upper teeth and according to him total disability of petitioner is 25%.
In the cross examination it is stated that petitioner has not taken any treatment regarding loss of teeth.
The disability in respect of teeth is disputed by the respondent.
It is necessary to notice that petitioner being finance officer, his teeth injury cannot come in the way of his occupation.
Further, in respect of teeth injury there is no medical record and it is also not mentioned in the wound certificate.
Therefore, in the opinion of this court, permanent disability of teeth cannot be considered to assess functional disability of the petitioner in the present case.
Having regard to (SCCH12) 10 MVC.No.7965/2019 fracture of nasal bone, restriction of movement of the right arm.
in the opinion of this court functional disability is 8% and to that extent compensation has to be awarded.

The quantum of compensation is determined as under:
(i) For Pain and sufferings: The petitioner has sustained injury which is grievous in nature.
The records show that he underwent surgery.
He was in hospital for 5 days with advice to take complete rest, continue medicine and to take follow up treatment.
As per the wound certificate one injury sustained by him is grievous in nature.
Therefore, for pain and suffering the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/ .
(ii) For Medical expenses: The petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.11 and 12.
He has taken treatment at Siddaganga hospital, Tumkur.
As per Ex.P. 11 and 12 medical bill, petitioner claims that he has paid Rs.86,483/. The said payment of bill is due to the accident caused to him.
They are subsequent to the date of accident.

Therefore, petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of Rs.86,483/.
(iii) For Food and nourishment:
The petitioner was in hospital for 5 days a per discharge summary produced at Ex.P.11.
Accident took place in the year 2019.
Since he was in hospital, food and nourishment charges will have to be awarded.
Considering the cost of living, and food, nourishment charges if per day Rs.200/ is awarded it will meet the ends of justice.
Hence for food and nourishment Rs.200/ x 05 days = Rs.1,000/is awarded.
For Attendant charges:
For a period of inpatient for 05 days some one should have looked after petitioner in the hospital.
Even if his family member has taken care of him in the said period, that family member's income for those days is lost.
Hence attendant charges has to be awarded.
if per day Rs.200/ is awarded as attendant charges in 2019, it will meet the ends of justice.
Hence for attendant charges Rs.200/ x 05 days =Rs.1,000/is awarded.
For Loss of income during laid up period:
As per the above findings, the income of the petitioner per month is Rs.13,000/.

In view of grievous injury minimum period of recovery can be 2 months and therefore, laid up period of petitioner is considered as total 2 months including in patient period and loss of income during laid up period is Rs.13,000/x 2 = Rs.26,
She is entitled to Rs.26,000/ as loss of income during laid up period.
(vi) Conveyance charges: It is stated that petitioner was shifted from spot of accident to the hospital.
He spent money for traveling to hospital.
Further he needs future medical treatment.
Considering those conveyances, in the opinion of this tribunal if an amount of Rs.5,000/ is awarded it will meet the ends of justice.

(vii) Loss of future income due to Disability : As per above findings the Functional disability of the petitioner is 8% and therefore loss of his future income due to disability is Rs.13,000/ income X 12 months X 8% disability X multiplier
It comes to Rs.2,24,640/.
Consequently, petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,24,640/ under the above head.
(viii) For Future medical expenses:
As per the evidence of doctor, implants are not removed and one surgery is necessary and Rs.60,000/ is required for such treatment.
But, no estimation is produced to rely up the said submission.
However, removal of implants is necessary for the well being of the patient.
Hence, in the opinion of this court Rs.25,000/ may be award for future medical expenses.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows: Particulars of Heads In Rs.

Therefore, I hold that the petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.3,89,123/ in respect of injuries sustained by her in t
Liability:
In the written statement of 1st respondent contended that driver of lorry KA01AF 2470 had no driving licence to drive the vehicle.
In the final report there is mention about lorry driver having no D.L at the time of accident.
Offence under Section 187 is registered against him.
The driver of the lorry has not summoned to produce his driving licence in the present case.

But,
since he has not produced driving licence charge U/Sec 187 of IMV Act is placed on him.

Driving the vehicle without having driving licence is violation of the terms of insurance policy in which case insurance company can be directed to pay the compensation and then it can recover it from the owner.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Shamanna and Another V/s Divisional Manager,
Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd and others, 2018 ACJ 2163, and in the case of New India Assurance Co.Ltd V/s Yallavva and Another, 2020 ACJ 2560
has held that insurance company can be directed to pay the compensation to the victim 3 rd party and then recover the said compensation amount from the owner.
The same is applicable to this case.
Therefore, 1 st respondent shall pay the compensation to petitioner and then recover the same from the owner of the vehicle respondent no.2 in terms of law.

Further as per the order sheet dated 12.07.2022 since petitioner remained absent for evidence for long time, my learned predecessorinoffice has ordered that petitioner is not entitled for interest on award amount from 12.07.2022 till he app
Hence, as per the said order petitioner is not entitled for interest on award amount from 12.07.2022 to 06.02.2023.

In view of above reasons I proceed to pass following :
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.3,89,123/ with interest @ 6% pa on the amount of Rs.3,64,123/from the date of petition till 12.07.2022 and from 06.02.2023 till the date of payment.
(Future medical expenses of Rs.25,000/ will not carry interest).

The respondent no.1 insurance  company is liable to indemnify the  insured and directed to deposit the  aforesaid compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this order.
